critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1627 lines — out-of-scope to refactor this iteration, but the ticket already flagged it. Splitting catalog/oem/admin routers into separate modules would help maintainability.
oem_search_variants currently only strips KIT/_S/_F/_XS — if other PSA pack codes appear (e.g. PACK, BTE, REC), they will not be peeled. Easy extension if/when needed.

cached_supplier_search is defined INSIDE the endpoint coroutine, which makes it hard to unit-test directly (had to copy the loop into the test). Consider hoisting it to module scope so it can be imported.

The variant loop uses 5 s asyncio.wait_for per variant — for a 4-variant ref (e.g. 1608747680_S) worst-case latency is 20 s if every supplier times out. Currently mitigated by Semaphore(25), but worth keeping an eye on tail latency in production.
Old supplier_lookup_cache rows (3126 of them) don't carry the matched_variant field yet — harmless (they will refresh under the 10 min TTL), just a heads-up.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug: TecDoc returns OEM refs in their canonical PSA/Renault form (10-digit, with KIT/_S suffixes, with leading zeros), but FadPro/Copia/PartsPro index the same physical article under one of several non-canonical forms (suffix-stripped, 6 or 8 leading digits, with/without a leading zero). Result: searching the canonical ref returns 0 hits even when the part exists. Mitigation (already shipped): server.oem_search_variants(ref) enumerates the variants in a sensible order (original → suffix-stripped → first-8 → first-6 → no-leading-zero → with-leading-zero), and cached_supplier_search iterates them, breaking on the first non-empty result, and stores the picked variant in db.supplier_lookup_cache.matched_variant so subsequent calls return identical items from cache. Verified live: 14 production rows in supplier_lookup_cache where matched_variant ≠ ref, including the exact ticket example (1610577780KIT → 1610577780).
